## `auth`

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth` | object | — | — | Login settings: the static user and the Dex connectors. See docs/configuration/authentication.md. |
| `auth.cookie` | object | — | — | The oauth2-proxy session cookie secret. |
| `auth.cookie.secretRef` | object | — | — | Secret in namespace oauth2-proxy with key cookie-secret. Keelson never creates it. Required with environment production. |
| `auth.cookie.secretRef.name` | string | — | not matching `^(oauth2-proxy\|dex-oidc-client)$` | Secret name. Not oauth2-proxy and not dex-oidc-client: those names are upstream's generated Secrets. |
| `auth.dex` | object | — | — | Dex settings. |
| `auth.dex.connectors` | array | — | — | Identity providers for Dex. Each connector needs domain. Static users off, or environment production, needs at least one. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].allowedGroups` | array | — | — | microsoft: only members may log in. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].emailToLowercase` | boolean | true | — | microsoft: Kubeflow compares user emails case-sensitively. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].extraConfig` | object | — | names match `^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`; names not matching `(?i)secret\|password\|token\|key` | Unsupported. Merged last into the connector config. No secret-like keys. ASCII letters, digits and _ only. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].groupNameFormat` | string | "name" | one of `name`, `id` | microsoft: return groups as names or as object IDs. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].groupsClaim` | string | "groups" | min length 1 | oidc: claim that Dex reads groups from. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].id` | string, required | — | max length 63; pattern `^[a-z0-9-]+$` | Unique. Also names the Dex env vars. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].issuer` | string | — | pattern `^https?://[^\s]+$` | oidc: issuer URL of the identity provider. Required for oidc. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].name` | string | — | min length 1 | Login button text. Default: id. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].onlySecurityGroups` | boolean | false | — | microsoft: return security groups only, no Microsoft 365 groups. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].orgs` | array | — | min 1 item | github: required, so arbitrary GitHub users can't log in. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].orgs[].name` | string, required | — | min length 1 | GitHub organization name. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].orgs[].teams` | array | — | — | Optional. Only members of one of these teams may log in. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].scopes` | array | — | min 1 item | oidc: scopes to request. Default: openid, profile, email, groups. Remove groups for providers that reject it. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].secretRef` | object, required | — | — | Secret in namespace auth with the client ID and client secret. Keelson never creates it. Put no secret values in values. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].secretRef.clientIDKey` | string | "clientID" | min length 1 | Key of the client ID in the Secret. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].secretRef.clientSecretKey` | string | "clientSecret" | min length 1 | Key of the client secret in the Secret. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].secretRef.name` | string, required | — | min length 1 | Secret in namespace auth. A name only. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].teamNameField` | string | "slug" | one of `name`, `slug`, `both` | github: how teams appear in groups: team name, team slug or both. Keelson default: slug. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].tenant` | string | — | pattern `^([0-9a-fA-F]{8}-([0-9a-fA-F]{4}-){3}[0-9a-fA-F]{12}\|[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?)+)$`; not matching `(?i)^(common\|consumers\|organizations)$` | microsoft: tenant ID or verified domain. A domain is lowercase only. Multi-tenant values accept any account and drop groups. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].type` | string, required | — | one of `oidc`, `microsoft`, `github` | Connector type: oidc (any OpenID Connect provider), microsoft (Entra ID) or github. |
| `auth.dex.connectors[].useLoginAsID` | boolean | false | — | github: use the GitHub login as the user ID, not the numeric ID. |
| `auth.oidcClient` | object | — | — | The OIDC client that oauth2-proxy uses to log in with Dex. Both components must read the same client ID and secret. |
| `auth.oidcClient.secretRef` | object | — | — | Secret with keys client-id and client-secret. Create it in both namespaces auth and oauth2-proxy. Keelson never creates it. Required with environment production. |
| `auth.oidcClient.secretRef.name` | string | — | not matching `^(oauth2-proxy\|dex-oidc-client)$` | Secret name. Not oauth2-proxy and not dex-oidc-client: those names are upstream's generated Secrets. |
| `auth.staticUsers` | object | — | — | Static user settings. |
| `auth.staticUsers.enabled` | boolean | — | — | Upstream static user user@example.com. Kind and dev only. |

## `tls`

| Key | Type | Default | Allowed | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tls` | object | — | — | Where HTTPS ends. See docs/configuration/domain-and-tls.md. |
| `tls.acme` | object | — | — | Let's Encrypt settings for issuer letsencrypt. See docs/configuration/domain-and-tls.md. |
| `tls.acme.dns01` | object | — | — | DNS-01 solver. v0.1 supports Azure DNS only. Required for letsencrypt. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS` | object | — | — | Azure DNS zone that holds domain. Set exactly one of managedIdentity or clientSecretRef. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.clientID` | string | — | min length 1 | Service principal: application (client) ID. Needs clientSecretRef. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.clientSecretRef` | object | — | — | Service principal: the Secret in the cert-manager namespace that holds the client secret. A name only. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.clientSecretRef.key` | string | — | min length 1 | Key in the Secret. Empty: client-secret. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.clientSecretRef.name` | string, required | — | min length 1 | Secret name in the cert-manager namespace. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.hostedZoneName` | string, required | — | min length 1 | Name of the DNS zone, for example example.com. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.managedIdentity` | object | — | — | Log in with a managed identity. No Secret. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.managedIdentity.clientID` | string, required | — | min length 1 | Client ID of the managed identity that may change the DNS zone. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.resourceGroupName` | string, required | — | min length 1 | Resource group of the DNS zone. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.subscriptionID` | string, required | — | min length 1 | Azure subscription ID of the DNS zone. |
| `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.tenantID` | string | — | min length 1 | Service principal: Microsoft Entra tenant ID. Needs clientSecretRef. |
| `tls.acme.email` | string | — | pattern `^$\|^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$` | Contact email of the ACME account. Let's Encrypt sends expiry notices to it. Required for letsencrypt. |
| `tls.acme.server` | string | "staging" | one of `staging`, `production` | staging: Let's Encrypt staging, not trusted by browsers, high rate limits. production: trusted certificates. Test with staging first. |
| `tls.issuer` | string | "none" | one of `none`, `existing`, `external`, `selfsigned`, `letsencrypt` | none: HTTP. existing: Istio terminates TLS with secretRef. external: TLS ends in front of the cluster; cookies are secure. selfsigned: Keelson issues a self-signed certificate (Secret keelson-tls). letsencrypt: Keelson issues a Let's Encrypt certificate with acme (Secret keelson-tls). |
| `tls.secretRef` | object | — | — | TLS Secret for issuer existing. A name only. |
| `tls.secretRef.name` | string | — | — | kubernetes.io/tls Secret in istio-system (issuer=existing). A name only, never key material. |

## Rules

The chart fails to render when one of these rules is broken.

- If `environment` is `production`, then `auth.cookie.secretRef.name` is not empty; `auth.dex.connectors` has at least 1 item; `auth.oidcClient.secretRef.name` is not empty; `auth.staticUsers.enabled` is `false`.
- If `auth.staticUsers.enabled` is `false`, then `auth.dex.connectors` has at least 1 item.
- If `auth.dex.connectors` has at least 1 item, then `domain` is not empty.
- If `tls.issuer` is `existing`, then `domain` is not empty; `tls.secretRef.name` is not empty.
- If `tls.issuer` is `external`, then `domain` is not empty.
- If `tls.issuer` is `selfsigned`, then `domain` is not empty.
- If `tls.issuer` is `letsencrypt`, then `domain` is not empty; `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS` is set; `tls.acme.email` is not empty.
- If `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.clientSecretRef` is set, then `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS` has none of the keys `managedIdentity`; `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.clientID` is set; `tls.acme.dns01.azureDNS.tenantID` is set.
- If `auth.dex.connectors[].type` is `oidc`, then `auth.dex.connectors[]` has none of the keys `tenant`, `allowedGroups`, `onlySecurityGroups`, `groupNameFormat`, `emailToLowercase`, `orgs`, `teamNameField`, `useLoginAsID`; `auth.dex.connectors[].issuer` is set.
- If `auth.dex.connectors[].type` is `microsoft`, then `auth.dex.connectors[]` has none of the keys `issuer`, `scopes`, `groupsClaim`, `orgs`, `teamNameField`, `useLoginAsID`; `auth.dex.connectors[].extraConfig` has no key matching `(?i)^(tenant\|groups\|useGroupsAsWhitelist)$`; `auth.dex.connectors[].tenant` is set.
- If `auth.dex.connectors[].type` is `github`, then `auth.dex.connectors[]` has none of the keys `issuer`, `scopes`, `groupsClaim`, `tenant`, `allowedGroups`, `onlySecurityGroups`, `groupNameFormat`, `emailToLowercase`; `auth.dex.connectors[].extraConfig` has no key matching `(?i)^(orgs?\|hostName\|rootCA)$`; `auth.dex.connectors[].orgs` is set.
